one_line: Carnatic music theorist and scholar at the 17th‑century Thanjavur Nayaka court, author of the Chaturdandi Prakashika.

appearance.age_look: late 40s, medium build, dignified scholar’s posture
appearance.face: oval face with warm brown complexion, sharp but gentle eyes, neatly trimmed black moustache, small vertical vibhuti lines on forehead with a central red tilaka, default expression calm and focused as if listening inwardly to music
appearance.hair: black hair parted at the centre, drawn back into a modest low bun at the nape; front kept smooth without loose strands; simple white cotton upper-cloth pulled over the head occasionally but normally no turban or cap, leaving the bun visible from behind
appearance.costume: era‑accurate 17th‑century South Indian Brahmin scholar dress: an off‑white hand‑woven cotton veshti/dhoti wrapped to ankle length with a neat narrow border in muted maroon, pleats in front; upper body covered by a full‑length, long‑sleeved, knee‑length angavastra‑style kurta in soft pale cream, slightly looser at the sleeves, worn under a separate pure‑white cotton uttariyam draped from left shoulder across the chest and around the back in a single broad fold; simple brown leather sandals; minimal jewellery limited to a thin gold chain barely visible at the neck and a pair of small gold studs in the ears, keeping the overall look austere and scholarly.
appearance.signature: a rolled palm‑leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark maroon cotton cord, with one loose palm leaf in his hand inscribed with tiny music‑theory notation marks, plus a small wooden stylus tucked visibly into the cord

ref_desc: Venkatamakhin is a late‑40s brown‑complexioned scholar with a calm, tilaka‑marked face, black hair in a low bun, cream kurta, off‑white veshti and uttariyam, carrying a maroon‑tied palm‑leaf manuscript and stylus in a warm off‑white, cream, maroon and brown palette.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character sheet of Venkatamakhin as a dignified 17th‑century Carnatic music theorist from Thanjavur: late‑40s, warm brown complexion, oval face, sharp but gentle eyes, neat black moustache, vertical vibhuti lines and a central red tilaka on his forehead, calm thoughtful expression. His black hair is parted in the centre and pulled back into a modest low bun at the nape, with the hair smooth at the front and no stray spikes. He wears an off‑white ankle‑length cotton veshti/dhoti with a narrow muted maroon border and front pleats, a pale cream long‑sleeved knee‑length kurta, and a separate pure‑white cotton uttariyam draped from his left shoulder across the chest and around the back in a broad fold; add simple brown leather sandals, a thin gold chain at the neck and small gold ear studs. In his hands and at his side show his signature prop: a rolled palm‑leaf manuscript bundle tied with a dark maroon cord, one loose inscribed palm leaf held for reading, and a small wooden stylus tucked into the cord. Use a restrained palette of off‑white, cream, warm brown, maroon and small gold accents, and present him front, three‑quarter and back views so his face, bun hairstyle, draped garments and manuscript bundle can be consistently redrawn.
